title: General Release of Claims
summary: One party gives up claims against another, usually in exchange for a payment.
useWhen: Settling a claim such as a minor accident, property damage or a contract dispute, where only one side is giving up claims. For two-way releases use the mutual release.
watchOuts: Personal injury releases should be signed only after the injured person understands the full extent of the injuries. Releasing claims early can waive future medical costs.
Minors generally cannot release their own claims, and parents' releases on behalf of minors are unenforceable in some states for some claims. Some settlements need court approval.

Releases of certain claims are restricted or need special steps: federal age-discrimination claims (OWBPA), wage-and-hour claims, workers' compensation, and claims of people receiving Medicare (Medicare secondary payer rules).
California requires an express waiver of Civil Code §1542 to release unknown claims. The template adds it when California law is chosen.

variables.label: Releasing party: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Released party: full legal name
variables.help: Full legal name of the person, or the exact registered name of the company.

variables.label: Claim or incident being released
variables.help: Describe it specifically: date, place, what happened, contract name.

variables.label: Payment due
variables.help: When the payment will be made.

variables.label: Scope
variables.default: claims arising from the incident only
options: claims arising from the incident only
all claims of any kind up to today
variables.help: A narrow release is easier to understand and enforce.

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 2. Payment
sections.body: In exchange for this release, Releasee will provide: {{consideration}}, by {{payment_due}}. Releasor confirms this is adequate consideration.

sections.title: 3. Release: incident only
sections.body: Releasor, for itself and its heirs, successors and assigns, releases Releasee and its owners, employees, agents, insurers, successors and assigns from all claims, demands, damages and causes of action, known or unknown, arising out of or relating to: {{incident}}.
sections.showIf: scope == 'claims arising from the incident only'

sections.title: 4. Release: all claims
sections.body: Releasor, for itself and its heirs, successors and assigns, releases Releasee and its owners, employees, agents, insurers, successors and assigns from all claims, demands, damages and causes of action of any kind, known or unknown, that exist up to the effective date, including those arising out of or relating to: {{incident}}.
sections.showIf: scope == 'all claims of any kind up to today'

sections.title: 5. What is not released
sections.body: This release does not cover obligations under this document, claims that arise after the effective date, or claims that cannot be released as a matter of law.

sections.title: 6. Waiver of California Civil Code §1542
sections.body: Releasor expressly waives the protection of California Civil Code §1542, which says: "A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party." Initials: [[initial:releasor]]

sections.title: 7. No admission
sections.body: This release is a compromise and is not an admission of liability by Releasee.

sections.title: 8. Releasor's confirmations
sections.body: Releasor confirms that Releasor (a) has not assigned any released claim to anyone, (b) has read and understands this release, (c) had the chance to consult a lawyer, and (d) signs voluntarily. Releasor will be responsible for any liens on the payment, such as medical or attorney liens, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing. Initials: [[initial:releasor]]

sections.title: 9. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Releasing party** — {{releasor_name}}

[[sig:releasor]]

Printed name: [[name:releasor]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:releasor:Title]]
Date: [[date:releasor]]

**Released party** — {{releasee_name}}

[[sig:releasee]]

Printed name: [[name:releasee]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:releasee:Title]]
Date: [[date:releasee]]
